name: rand SmallRng (Xoshiro256++ on 64-bit)
verdict_reason: Rand's guide lists Xoshiro256++, SmallRng's algorithm on 64-bit targets, at 11 GB/s against 4.1 GB/s for ChaCha12 on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D, and an independent M1 Max run measured 1.13 ns vs 4.11 ns per u64. SmallRng is not the fastest small generator: wyrand crates such as fastrand are about 2x faster again.
tier_reason: The rand book's figures are first-party and rough, but an independent criterion run on a stated CPU agrees.
claimed_speedup: u64 output: 11 GB/s vs 4.1 GB/s for ChaCha12 (Ryzen 9 9950X3D, rand book); one u64: 1.13 ns vs 4.11 ns, fill 1 KiB: 7.05 GB/s vs 2.02 GB/s (Apple M1 Max)
workload: u64 generation; second source also measures u32 draws and filling a 1 KiB buffer.
hardware: AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D (rand book); Apple M1 Max (rapidrand)
platforms: All targets; Xoshiro256++ on 64-bit, Xoshiro128++ on 32-bit
one_liner: rand's non-cryptographic SmallRng: about 2.7x to 3.6x faster than the ChaCha12 generator behind StdRng and rand::rng().
how_it_is_fast: Xoshiro256++ updates 32 bytes of state with a few shifts, rotates and XORs and adds two words for output, so each u64 costs a handful of instructions. ChaCha12 runs 12 rounds of a cipher block function and buffers the output.
use_it_when: Simulations, games and randomized algorithms already written against rand's traits and distributions
Seeding many independent fast generators from one ThreadRng
skip_it_when: Anything security-relevant: use rand::rng() or StdRng
Reproducible streams across rand versions: SmallRng is documented as non-portable; use rand_xoshiro directly
Maximum speed outside the rand ecosystem: fastrand measured 0.51 ns vs 1.13 ns per u64
caveats: The rand book calls its numbers rough and limited to u64 output
The book gives no number for SmallRng itself, only for Xoshiro256++, which the docs name as its current 64-bit algorithm
tradeoffs: Algorithm may change between rand versions

evidence.quote: Here, performance is measured roughly for u64 outputs on an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D
Xoshiro256PlusPlus on 64-bit platforms and Xoshiro128PlusPlus on 32-bit
The current algorithm used is the ChaCha block cipher with 12 rounds.
